## Saturation adjustment inside a snapy stage (thermodynamics card) {#sec-ch14-saturation}

### Summary

At the end of the last stage of its time integrator, snapy brings the condensable species back to phase
equilibrium by calling kintera's saturation adjustment at fixed density and internal energy. This section derives
what the call holds fixed and shows that total mass, every element and the internal energy are conserved across
it, and that the latent heat appears as a warming when snapy next inverts the energy for the temperature. It also
states what happens to a cell whose adjustment does not converge: the cell is counted, its partly adjusted state is
still written, and snapy redoes the step with a smaller time step.

::: {.callout-note title="At a glance"}
**Purpose.** Phase equilibrium of @sec-ch04 at fixed density and internal energy, in place on the mass fractions;
budgets @eq-ch14-saturation-mass and @eq-ch14-saturation-elements.

**Data.** Density [$\mathrm{kg\,m^{-3}}$], internal energy [$\mathrm{J\,m^{-3}}$], mass fractions [-] (updated).

**Placement.** End of the last snapy stage; failure count read by snapy's redo check.

**Activation.** A moist equation of state whose card has nucleation reactions; warm start on.

**Guarantee / limits.** Mass and elements exact for cards whose phase changes keep the molar mass; failed cells are
counted, not raised.

**Evidence.** `check_ch14_coupling.py` lines (k) to (r); see the Tests layer.
:::

Local symbols: $\rho$, total density; $\rho_0$, dry density; $y_i$, $y_i'$, mass fractions before and after; $U$,
internal energy per volume; $c$, $c'$, concentrations before and after; $S$, the stoichiometric matrix with entries
$S_{ij}$; $\xi_j$, extent of reaction $j$ per volume; $a_{ei}$, atoms of element $e$ in species $i$; $\mu_i$, molar
mass; $T$, $T'$, temperature before and after.

### Derivation

**What snapy passes.** snapy forms $\rho = \rho_0 + \sum_i \rho_i$, the internal energy $U = E - e_k$ and
$y_i = \rho_i/\rho$, and calls its `forward` on the interior cells with warm start
([`snapy meshblock.cpp:816-835`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/f93b1cf12819be2d310f8aa84fb74cc627e9ac70/src/mesh/meshblock.cpp#L816-L835)). Afterwards it writes $\rho_i = y_i' \rho$ (`yfrac` times `rho`) and leaves the dry row and $E$ as
they were ([`snapy meshblock.cpp:837`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/f93b1cf12819be2d310f8aa84fb74cc627e9ac70/src/mesh/meshblock.cpp#L837)). Inside, kintera solves one UV equilibrium in concentrations with
the molar energies and heat capacities converted from the per-mass buffers, then returns
$\rho_i = \mu_i c_i'$ and overwrites $y$ with `V->Y`, which divides by the new $\sum_i \rho_i$
({{< code src/thermo/thermo_y.cpp ThermoYImpl::forward >}}, {{< code src/thermo/thermo_y.cpp ThermoYImpl::_ivol_to_yfrac >}}).

**Step 1: what is held.** The cell has a fixed volume and no heat is added during the call, so the first law gives
$\mathrm dU = 0$: the solver holds $U$ and the density, and moves the composition along the reactions,
$c' = c + S\xi$ (@sec-ch04-equilibrate-uv).

**Step 2: the dry gas.** The dry species is in no reaction, so $c_0' = c_0$ and $\rho_0$ is unchanged; the dry row
snapy leaves untouched is therefore still right.

**Step 3: total mass.** The mass per volume changes by $\sum_i \mu_i (c_i' - c_i) = \sum_j \xi_j \sum_i \mu_i S_{ij}$.
When the molar masses come from the compositions, every phase change has the same molar mass on both sides, so

$$
\sum_i \mu_i S_{ij} = 0 \ \text{for every reaction } j \quad\Rightarrow\quad \sum_i \rho_i' = \sum_i \rho_i = \rho ,
$$ {#eq-ch14-saturation-mass}

and `V->Y` divides by the incoming $\rho$. Writing $\rho_i = y_i' \rho$ with the incoming $\rho$ is then exact.

**Step 4: elements.** The element moles change by $\sum_i a_{ei} (c_i' - c_i) = \sum_j \xi_j \sum_i a_{ei} S_{ij}$, so

$$
\sum_i a_{ei} c_i' = \sum_i a_{ei} c_i \ \text{for every element } e \quad \text{when} \quad \sum_i a_{ei} S_{ij} = 0 ,
$$ {#eq-ch14-saturation-elements}

which holds for balanced reactions (@sec-ch01b-state). `forward` moves the composition only along the columns of
$S$ ({{< code src/thermo/thermo_y.cpp ThermoYImpl::forward >}}), so both budgets follow from the stoichiometry.

**Step 5: where the latent heat goes.** snapy keeps $E$, and so $U$. The condensates carry lower offsets $u_i^0$ in
@eq-ch14-thermo-energy, so moving mass from vapour to condensate at fixed $U$ leaves more thermal energy. That
warming appears when snapy next inverts $U$ for $T$ (`VU->T`,
[`snapy moist_mixture.cpp:150`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/f93b1cf12819be2d310f8aa84fb74cc627e9ac70/src/eos/moist_mixture.cpp#L150)); the adjustment itself writes no temperature.

**Step 6: one energy on both sides.** The energy snapy holds and the energy kintera conserves are the same function
for `moist-mixture`, and for `ideal-moist` with a linear card (@sec-ch14-thermo, @eq-ch14-thermo-ideal-moist). With
NASA-9 data or the H$_2$ heat capacity under `ideal-moist` they differ, and the temperature after the adjustment is
not the equilibrium temperature: suspect S14-3, latent (@sec-ch14-thermo, Limits).

**Step 7: non-convergence.** A cell that does not converge has `diag < 0`. `forward` adds it to a failure count on
the cells' device, warns on CPU, and still writes the partly adjusted concentrations back
({{< code src/thermo/thermo_y.cpp ThermoYImpl::forward >}}). Each Newton update is a stoichiometric step, so the
written state is still on the conservation manifold of Steps 3 and 4. snapy's redo check (`check_redo`) reads the
count tensor `nfail_` directly and resets it ([`snapy meshblock.cpp:1363-1365`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/f93b1cf12819be2d310f8aa84fb74cc627e9ac70/src/mesh/meshblock.cpp#L1363-L1365)), stacks it as the
saturation flag with `stack` ([`:1374-1375`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/f93b1cf12819be2d310f8aa84fb74cc627e9ac70/src/mesh/meshblock.cpp#L1374-L1375)), and sets bit 16 of the redo `causes` in the reduction
([`:1406`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/f93b1cf12819be2d310f8aa84fb74cc627e9ac70/src/mesh/meshblock.cpp#L1406)); the step is then redone with a smaller time step, which discards the written state. The read is
a tensor comparison on the cells' device, so `forward` does not synchronise on CUDA; the redo check copies its whole
flag vector to the host once, afterwards (`read_redo_flags`). `take_saturation_adjustment_failures` is the host-side drain: it returns the count
with `.item()` and resets it ({{< code src/thermo/thermo_y.cpp ThermoYImpl::take_saturation_adjustment_failures >}}),
and snapy calls it once before the step, through `saturation_failures` ([`snapy meshblock.cpp:637`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/f93b1cf12819be2d310f8aa84fb74cc627e9ac70/src/mesh/meshblock.cpp#L637),
`take_saturation_adjustment_failures` at [`:1269-1276`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/f93b1cf12819be2d310f8aa84fb74cc627e9ac70/src/mesh/meshblock.cpp#L1269-L1276)), so that a failure counted before the step is not taken as its own. The temperature
inversions `VU->T` and `PV->T` only warn when they reach their iteration limit and are not counted
({{< code src/thermo/thermo_y.cpp ThermoYImpl::_intEng_to_temp >}}, {{< code src/thermo/thermo_y.cpp ThermoYImpl::_pres_to_temp >}};
Limits).

The check runs the adjustment with inputs built as snapy builds them on the Jupiter deck (it skips snapy's conserved
limiter and sets the kinetic energy to zero), in six supersaturated cells from 140 K to
300 K.[^ch14-check-sat]

- "(k) adjustment moved mass fractions by up to 1.00e+00 of the largest (state was supersaturated) PASS"
- "(l) total density rho_dry + sum y' rho equals rho (dry row untouched): max rel err 2.22e-16 (tol 1e-14) PASS"
- "(m) element moles H, He, N, O, S per cell conserved: max rel err 3.69e-16 (tol 1e-13) PASS"
- "(n) snapy's next VU->T at fixed ie (meshblock.cpp:825) = linear-model T: max rel err 2.22e-16 (tol 1e-12) PASS"
- "(o) latent warming T' - T per cell [K]: 28.163 27.660 26.127 18.686 11.822 4.714 INFO"
- "(p) max relative humidity per cell at (T', p') after the adjustment: 1.000000 1.000000 1.000000 1.000000 1.000000 1.000000 INFO"
- "(k0) diag per cell at the default max_iter 100 (negative = failed): 11 9 9 7 5 4 INFO"
- "(q) max_iter = 1: 6 failed cell(s) counted, count reset to 0 on the second read PASS"
- "(r) failed cells: written state still conserves total density: max rel err 2.22e-16 (tol 1e-14) PASS"

Line (k0) shows all six cells converging at the default limit of 100 iterations. Line (q) deliberately reduces
that limit to 1 and verifies the failure count. With an explicit limit of 10, the first cell reports failure,
but all six warming values in line (o) are unchanged at the printed 0.001 K precision.[^ch14-iteration-control]

No published derivation is quoted. The steps are the first law at fixed volume and the stoichiometry of
@sec-ch04, matched to the code at the two pins.

### Numerical method

The adjustment is the UV solver of @sec-ch04-equilibrate-uv, called once per step on the interior cells. The
figure is not provided: the figure module is not written yet.

### Limits

- @eq-ch14-saturation-mass needs every phase change to keep the molar mass. A card whose vapour and condensate get
  their molar masses from different compositions loses or gains mass at every adjustment; kintera's readers do not
  reject such a card (@sec-ch14-thermo, Limits).
- `VU->T` and `PV->T` report non-convergence only as a warning, so snapy's redo check cannot see it. For the linear
  model both converge in one step (@sec-ch14-thermo); the gap matters only with NASA-9, H$_2$ or compressibility
  terms. This is suspect S14-4, latent, recorded as row K26 of the issue below.[^ch14-k26]
